title: Bounded below cochain complexes localize to the bounded below derived category
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], with derived category $Q:\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] in the chosen universe. Let $\mathrm{CoCh}^+(\mathcal A)$ be the full subcategory of integer-indexed cochain complexes $K$ for which there exists $n\in\mathbf Z$ with $K^r=0$ for all $r<n$, and let $K^+(\mathcal A)$ be their homotopy category (morphisms of complexes modulo chain homotopy). Let $q^+:\mathrm{CoCh}^+(\mathcal A)\to K^+(\mathcal A)$ be the quotient functor and $Q_h^+:K^+(\mathcal A)\to D^+(\mathcal A)$ the functor induced by the homotopy-to-derived localization, with $D^+(\mathcal A)$ the strictly full subcategory of $D(\mathcal A)$ whose cohomology vanishes in all sufficiently negative degrees [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Then $Q^+=Q_h^+\circ q^+$ is a localization at quasi-isomorphisms: it inverts them, and for every category $\mathcal E$ precomposition with $Q^+$ is an equivalence from the category of functors $D^+(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal E$ to the full subcategory of functors $\mathrm{CoCh}^+(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal E$ that invert quasi-isomorphisms. Moreover, if $i_C:\mathrm{CoCh}^+(\mathcal A)\to\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal A)$ and $i_D:D^+(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ are the inclusions, there is a canonical natural isomorphism $i_D\circ Q^+\cong Q\circ i_C$, given by the quotient-to-derived comparison on each bounded below complex.
